title: Friedmann equation, flat universe
references: Friedmann, A., Ueber die Kruemmung des Raumes, Zeitschrift fuer Physik 10, 377-386 (1922), doi:10.1007/BF01332580
Ryden, B., Introduction to Cosmology, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press
validity_domain: Expansion rate H of a homogeneous, isotropic (FLRW) universe with zero spatial curvature (k = 0), H^2 = 8 pi G rho / 3, where rho is the total mass-energy density of all components divided by c^2, including dark energy treated as an effective density.
limitations: Flat universe only: for k not zero the term -k c^2 / a^2 is not included, so the law does not apply
rho is the total density of every component (matter, radiation, dark energy as an effective density); the value of a single component is not enough
H and rho refer to the same epoch; the law does not give H today unless rho is the density today
H is in s^-1 (unit Hz); a claim in km/s/Mpc must be converted first, that unit is not in the core units table
A model of homogeneous cosmology, not a statement about local structure

variables.rho: Total mass-energy density divided by c squared
